2019_133_050719spmtg.paragraph: A special meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education was called for May 7, 2019 at 5:30 PM at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, with a single business item: consideration of Custodial, Grounds and Warehouse Services. The packet contains a resolution selecting D.M. Burr to perform the district's custodial, grounds and warehouse services under a Request for Proposals issued March 21, 2019, and authorizing the Superintendent or his designee to negotiate, finalize and execute the contract subject to legal counsel review. A May 3, 2019 memorandum from Assistant Superintendent Rick West recommends D.M. Burr at a beginning custodial wage of $13 per hour.

**Meeting**
Special Meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, May 7, 2019, 5:30 PM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. District phone 248.823.4000; web site www.troy.k12.mi.us. Board of Education meetings are cablecast when school is in session on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and may be viewed online at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Agenda**
1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Public Communication; 3. Business — A. Consideration: Custodial, Grounds & Warehouse Services; 4. Adjournment. The notice states items do not have to be taken in the order shown, and that items within the consent agenda are acted on at one time unless removed.

**Business item and resolution**
Bids were opened April 4, 2019 for third party contracting of Custodial Services. The recommended action is to accept a resolution reciting that, to maintain the School District's goal of 100% of stakeholders responding positively to the quality of their learning environment and to ensure resources are directed to high quality educational services and programs, the Board issued a Request for Proposals for Custodial, Grounds and Warehouse Services on March 21, 2019. After comprehensive review and analysis of the proposals received, the Board concludes it can maintain and enhance the level, mix and quality of services by contracting with D.M. Burr. The resolution (1) selects D.M. Burr to perform the custodial, grounds and warehouse services as set forth in the RFP, and (2) authorizes the Superintendent or his designee to negotiate and finalize the contract terms subject to review and approval by the School District's legal counsel, and to execute the resulting contract with D.M. Burr Group and any incidental documents. The Moved by, Supported by, Yes and No lines are blank, and the adopted/defeated designation is unmarked. A certification block for the Secretary of the Board of Education attests compliance with the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976.

**Procurement history (memorandum of May 3, 2019)**
From Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, to Dr. Rich Machesky, Superintendent of Schools, copy to Rob Carson, Director of Operations. Business Office, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; phone 248.823.4022; fax 248.823.4013. RFP #9881 for Custodial, Grounds & Warehouse Services was issued March 21, 2019; proposals were due April 4, 2019 and five competitive proposals were received. Rob Carson, Larry Franckowiak and Rick West reviewed and analyzed the submissions and selected ABM, D.M. Burr and GDI to interview.

**Interviews**
On April 18, 2019 a committee interviewed the three selected companies, each for approximately one hour, including presentations and a Q&A session. Committee members: Nicole Wilson, Bob Dowd, Joe Duda, Sarah Glasser, Larry Franckowiak, Rob Carson, Jim Crowley and Rick West. The committee was not a decision-making body. General discomfort was conveyed with GDI's proposal and presentation; the committee did not feel GDI demonstrated the relevant K-12 experience needed and eliminated the firm from further consideration. Both ABM and D.M. Burr were viewed as qualified.

**Overtime and wage findings**

| Firm | Assumed billable overtime | Effect of direct pass-through billing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D.M. Burr | 3,000 hours | Proposed price reduced by $124,000 |
| ABM | None included | Price firm |

Carson and West believe it is in the district's best interest for the successful contractor to bill overtime hours as a direct pass through rather than including them in the contract price. The RFP asked each company to cost out its proposal at $12, $13 and $14 beginning wages for custodians; each company stated the current labor market in Troy would require a $13 minimum wage to recruit and retain custodians.

**Recommendation and attachments**
West recommends the Board approve a resolution allowing staff to negotiate a successor contract with D.M. Burr for Custodial, Grounds and Warehouse Services at a beginning custodial wage of $13 per hour, at the Special Meeting on May 7, 2019. Attachments listed: Custodial, Grounds & Warehouse Services Tabulation, and Troy – Resolution Authorizing Custodial, Grounds and Warehouse Services Contract (2019).

It notes that when school is in session, Board of Education meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and that School Board meetings can also be viewed online at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. AGENDA. The special meeting agenda has four items: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Public Communication; 3. Business, consisting of a single item, A. Consideration: Custodial, Grounds & Warehouse Services; and 4. Adjournment.

BUSINESS ITEM 3.A — CONSIDERATION: CONTRACTED SERVICES - CUSTODIAL (dated 05.07.19). The item states that bids were opened on April 4, 2019 for third party contracting of Custodial Services, and presents a resolution for board consideration regarding privatization. The recommended action is to accept the resolution.

SUGGESTED RESOLUTION. The resolution form contains blank lines for "Moved by" and "Supported by." Its first WHEREAS clause recites that, in order to maintain the School District's goal of 100% of stakeholders responding positively to the quality of their learning environment, and to ensure School District resources are directed to the maintenance of high quality educational services and programs for its students, the Board of Education issued a Request for Proposals for Custodial, Grounds and Warehouse Services on March 21, 2019 (the "RFP"). The second WHEREAS clause recites that after a comprehensive review and analysis of the proposals received in response to the RFP, the Board of Education concluded it can maintain and enhance the level, mix and quality of the custodial, grounds and warehouse services of the School District's facilities through contracting for the School District's custodial, grounds and warehouse operations with D.M. Burr.

The resolving clauses provide: (1) the School District hereby selects D.M. Burr to perform the custodial, grounds and warehouse services of the School District as set forth in the RFP; and (2) the Superintendent or his designee is authorized to (a) negotiate and finalize the terms and conditions of the contract with D.M. Burr, subject to the review and approval by the School District's legal counsel, and (b) execute the resulting contract with D.M. Burr Group, as well as any and all documents necessary and incidental to said contract, on behalf of the School District.

The resolution includes blank "Yes:" and "No:" tally lines and the line "Motion to adopt resolution ADOPTED / DEFEATED on May 7, 2019," with neither outcome marked and no mover, supporter or vote recorded in the packet copy. A signature line for the Secretary, Board of Education follows. A certification block states: "I hereby certify that the foregoing constitutes a true and complete copy of a resolution duly adopted by the Board of Education of the Troy School District of Troy, Michigan, at regular meeting held on the 7th day of May, 2019," and that said meeting was conducted and public notice given pursuant to and in full compliance with the Open Meeting Act, being Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976, and that the minutes of said meeting were kept and will be or have been made available as required by that Act. A second Secretary, Board of Education signature line follows.

SUPPORTING MEMORANDUM. A memorandum dated May 3, 2019 is addressed TO Dr. Rich Machesky, Superintendent of Schools, FROM Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, with a copy to Rob Carson, Director of Operations. The letterhead identifies the Business Office at 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, phone 248.823.4022, fax 248.823.4013. The subject line reads: Custodial, Grounds, Warehouse Services RFP.

Solicitation. The memorandum states the district issued Request for Proposals (RFP) #9881 for Custodial, Grounds & Warehouse Services on March 21, 2019. Proposals were due April 4, 2019, and five (5) competitive proposals were received. Rob Carson, Larry Franckowiak and Rick West reviewed and analyzed the submitted proposals and selected ABM, D.M. Burr and GDI to interview.

Interviews. On April 18, 2019 a committee conducted interviews of the three selected companies. The committee consisted of Nicole Wilson, Bob Dowd, Joe Duda, Sarah Glasser, Larry Franckowiak, Rob Carson, Jim Crowley and Rick West. Each company was provided approximately a one-hour interview in which it presented its proposal and engaged in a Q&A session with the committee. The memorandum notes each committee member brought a unique perspective and provided valuable input to assist in making a recommendation.

Evaluation outcome. Although the committee was not a decision-making body, a general level of discomfort was conveyed with the proposal and presentation submitted by GDI. The committee did not feel GDI demonstrated the relevant K-12 experience needed to service the District, and therefore eliminated GDI from further consideration. The committee felt that both ABM and D.M. Burr were qualified to service the District. The committee discussed the cost associated with both proposals and each member's experience with transitioning service providers, and recommended that Rob Carson and Rick West further review the costs of each proposal and explore the possibility of negotiating a successor agreement with DM Burr.

Overtime treatment. In further reviewing the costs associated with the ABM and DM Burr proposals, the district asked both companies to provide the number of assumed overtime hours in their proposals needed to adequately cover all events requested by the District, and a new proposed number if the District were to bill overtime as a direct pass through. DM Burr responded that it had assumed 3,000 hours of billable overtime and reduced its proposed price by $124,000 if overtime were billed as a direct pass through. ABM responded that it did not include any billable overtime hours and that its price was firm. Rob Carson and Rick West state their belief that it is in the district's best interest to have the successful contractor begin to bill overtime hours as a direct pass through as opposed to including overtime in the contract price.

Wage structure. The RFP asked each company to cost out its proposal at a $12, $13 and $14 beginning wage for custodians. The memorandum notes that each of the companies stated that the current labor market in Troy would require a $13 minimum wage to recruit and retain custodians.

Recommendation. Citing the process described, the conversations held, and the combined experience in custodial contract management, West recommends the Board of Education approve a resolution allowing staff to negotiate a successor contract with D.M. Burr for Custodial, Grounds, and Warehouse Services with a beginning custodial wage of $13 per hour, at a Special Meeting on May 7, 2019. He states he has included the cost proposals for each of the three companies along with the recommended resolution, and invites questions, comments or concerns.

Attachments. Two attachments are listed: "Custodial, Grounds & Warehouse Services Tabulation" and "Troy – Resolution Authorizing Custodial, Grounds and Warehouse Services Contract (2019)." The final pages of the packet, which correspond to the cost tabulation attachment, contain no extractable text beyond their page numbers, so the per-firm bid amounts referenced in the memorandum are not reproduced in the document text.
